rl-wa-spring.back: Spring: groundwater flowing out on its own. Seep: water oozing slowly over a damp patch.

rl-wa-where-spring.back: Where a slope eases: the toe of a bench or the head of a draw, where water running along a tight layer comes out.

rl-wa-dashed.back: An intermittent creek: it may be dry.

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="How water looks on the Hunt Map Topo base: a solid blue line for a creek that flows all year, a dashed blue line for an intermittent creek that may be dry, a pale green grey fill for wetlands, and blue fill for lakes and ponds.   <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>

rl-wa-missing.front: Do maps show every spring and seep?
rl-wa-missing.back: No. Many are missing. Use the Satellite base, plants and your boots.

rl-wa-green.front: In a dry October, what marks water on a brown hill?
rl-wa-green.back: The greenest spot: aspen clumps, willow, dogwood, brushy draws.

rl-wa-plants.front: Four plants that point to water?
rl-wa-plants.back: Willow, red osier dogwood, cottonwood, aspen (also alder, sedge, cattail).

rl-wa-dugout.front: Ranch dugout full of ducks: first step?
rl-wa-dugout.back: Permission, and no hunting or shooting within 100 m of an occupied dwelling or farm building.
